context: A doctor explains a wellness research summary to a teen
purpose: Teach: 公判/判事/ノーベル/飼育/曲線/半数/根底/療養

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 先生、最近よく眠れなくて。学校から帰ると、もうへとへとなんです。
lines.en: Doctor, I haven't been sleeping well lately. By the time I get home from school, I'm already exhausted.
lines.style: Tired teen voice, slightly drawn-out vowels, opening up to a trusted adult

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: なるほど。実はね、ノーベル賞をとった先生のチームが、疲れの曲線について面白い研究をしているんだよ。
lines.en: I see. Actually, a team led by a Nobel-winning professor has done some interesting research on the curve of fatigue.
lines.style: Warm doctor voice, easing into the topic gently, slowing on technical terms

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 疲れに曲線があるんですか？なんか、グラフみたいでちょっと面白いですね。
lines.en: Fatigue has a curve? That sounds kind of interesting, like a graph or something.
lines.style: Curious teen tone, voice perking up with mild surprise

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: そう、毎日同じ時間に寝るだけで、調べた高校生の半数くらいが、二週間で楽になったんだ。
lines.en: Right — and just by going to bed at the same time every day, about half of the high schoolers they studied felt better within two weeks.
lines.style: Encouraging, practical example, voice lifting on the hopeful statistic

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 半数も？じゃあ、わたしも試せそうかも。寝る時間ってそんなに根底から効くんですね。
lines.en: Half of them? Then maybe I could try it too. So bedtime really matters at a fundamental level, huh.
lines.style: Brightening teen voice, hopeful realization, casual phrasing

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: うん、生活リズムは健康の根底にあるからね。あと、犬とか猫の飼育もストレスを下げるって言われてるよ。
lines.en: Yes, daily rhythm is at the foundation of health. Also, keeping a dog or cat is said to reduce stress.
lines.style: Friendly mentor tone, adding a relatable example with a soft smile in the voice

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: あ、それニュースで見ました！どこかの判事さんが、公判の合間に保護犬と過ごして救われたって話。
lines.en: Oh, I saw that on the news! Some judge talked about being saved by spending time with a rescue dog between court sessions.
lines.style: Lively teen recognition, animated and slightly excited to share what she saw

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: ああ、あの記事ね。公判が続くと判事さんも本当に疲れるから、動物との時間が効くんだろうね。
lines.en: Ah, that article. Trials drag on, so judges really do get exhausted — time with animals must help.
lines.style: Pleased recognition, conversational and knowing, connecting threads naturally

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: うちもおばあちゃんが自宅療養してて、猫がいると表情がやわらかいんです。
lines.en: My grandma is recuperating at home too, and when the cat's around, her expression really softens.
lines.style: Tender teen voice, sharing something personal, slightly slower and softer

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: それは素敵だね。療養中はとくに、そういう小さなことが一番効いたりするんだよ。
lines.en: That's lovely. Especially during recuperation, those small things often help the most.
lines.style: Warm closing tone from doctor, affirming and gentle, wrapping up kindly
